BMDM1.claim: The Meenakshi Amman Temple has 14 towers of 45–50 metres and a thousand-pillared hall with musical pillars.

evidence.quote: It is quite an architectural marvel with 14 temple towers with a height ranging between 45-50 metres.
A 1000 pillared hall is another major feature with exquisitely sculpted pillars. There are musical pillars which produce sounds of different scales.

BMDM4.claim: Darshan hours are 6:00 am to 12:30 pm and 4:00 pm to 9:00 pm; early morning is the best time to visit.

evidence.quote: Morning Hours: 6:00 am to 12:30 pm; Evening Hours: 4:00 pm to 9:00 pm.
The best time to visit the temple is early morning

BMDN1.claim: King Thirumalai Nayak built the palace in 1635, blending Dravidian and foreign styles; it is protected by the Archaeological department.

evidence.quote: Built in 1635 by the King Thirumalai Nayak, it is a master piece combining Dravidian and foreign architectural styles with elan.
This is now being protected by the Archaeological department.

BMDN2.claim: The palace has two sections, Swarga Vilasam and Ranga Vilasam, a vast central courtyard, painted ceilings and an evening light and sound show.

evidence.quote: The palace has two sections; Swarga vilasam and Ranga vilasam.
Majestic pillars, the massive central courtyard and dancing hall are sure to leave you spell bound.
The light and sound shows held in the evening make for a doubly alluring experience.

BMDG1.claim: The Gandhi Memorial Museum is in Rani Mangammal's palace of 1670, with a replica of a Sevagram hut in front.

evidence.quote: Gandhi Memorial museum is housed in the splendid old palace of Rani Mangammal.
The palace which now houses the museum was built during the Naick reign in 1670 AD.
A replica of a hut in Sevagram sits in front of the main building of the museum.

BMDG2.claim: About 100 objects used by Gandhi are on show, including the blood-stained cloth he wore on the day he was assassinated.

evidence.quote: The third section displays around 100 artifacts which were used by Mahatma Gandhi.
a blood stained cloth worn by Gandhi on the day he was assassinated are included among these artifacts.

BMDT1.claim: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam, 2 km from the Meenakshi temple, is a vast temple tank of 1645 with a shrine on an island in the middle.

evidence.quote: the place is just 2 kms away from the Meenakshi Sundareswara temple.
Surrounded by granite steps on four sides, the temple is in the middle of the pond.
This stunning pond was created in 1645 AD during the reign of Thirumalai Nayak.

BMDT2.claim: The tank is the venue of Madurai's float festival in January/February, when the deities are carried on a lit float.

evidence.quote: This pond is the main venue of the famous float festival held in January / February.
The deities of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar are carried to the pond in a float called Teppam.

BMD3.claim: Madurai airport has flights to Colombo, Dubai and Singapore and to Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Delhi; Madurai Junction is the main station.

evidence.quote: The airport has direct connectivity with international destinations like Colombo, Dubai and Singapore.
It is also well connected with popular domestic destinations like Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai and New Delhi.
Madurai Junction is the major railway station serving the city.

BMD4.claim: Madurai has three bus terminals: Mattuthavani (M.G.R.), Arappalayam for intercity buses, and Periyar for city buses.

evidence.quote: Madurai has three bus terminals - M.G.R. Bus Stand (Mattuthavani), Arappalayam (for inter city buses) and Periyar Bus Stand (for intra city buses).

BMD5.claim: Madurai can be visited year-round, but December to February is the most comfortable.

evidence.quote: It is a destination that can be visited any time of the year. However, for the best experience, visit the destination during December to February.

BMD6.claim: The Samanar hills near Keelakuyilkudi have Jain and Hindu monuments across a stretch of rocky hillocks.

evidence.quote: History, culture, and nature come together at Samanar hills, a rocky stretch of hillocks, known for its many Jain and Hindu monuments dotted across its landscape.

DU1.claim: Madurai is called Thoonga Nagaram, 'the city that never sleeps', and Incredible India calls it the Athens of the East.

evidence.quote: is what Madurai is popularly called in Tamil Nadu.
It is often referred to as the Athens of the East for its architectural grandeur and cultural richness.

DU2.claim: Madurai was the seat of the Tamil Sangam, the assemblies of Tamil poets and scholars.

evidence.quote: Sangam, the confluence of Tamil scholars and critics, used to regularly convene in the city
The earliest references of Madurai can be traced back to the 3rd century BC.

DU3.claim: Thirumalai Nayak Palace blends Dravidian and Islamic styles and has 248 pillars.

evidence.quote: where Dravidian and Islamic styles converge seamlessly.
to 248 majestic pillars, the palace exhibits sheer magnificence.

DU4.claim: The Teppakulam is the largest temple tank in Tamil Nadu.

evidence.quote: a sacred oasis with the largest temple tank in the state.

DU5.claim: In January the three-day Pongal harvest festival includes Jallikattu, the bull-taming sport, in villages around Madurai.

evidence.quote: The year begins with Pongal, a 3-day Harvest Festival
The Jallikattu festival, a spellbinding bull-taming sport is part of the Pongal festival celebrations.

DU6.claim: The ten-day Chithirai festival in April–May celebrates the wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar and draws about a million visitors.

evidence.quote: celebrated during April–May every year, attracts 1 million visitors.

DU7.claim: Madurai's food includes jigarthanda, paruthipal, kothu parotta, kari dosai (dosa topped with spiced mutton) and appam.

evidence.quote: From the exclusive drink of Madurai, Paruthipal, made from cotton seeds and jaggery, to the beloved street-side dish, Kuthuparotta
Dive into the unique fusion of Indian and pizza-like elements with Kari Dosai
Cool off with the refreshing flavours of Jigarthanda, Madurai's famous cold beverage

DU8.claim: Madurai's flower market is famous for malligai jasmine.

evidence.quote: Delight your senses at the amazing flower market in Madurai, where you'll find the world-famous Malligai Jasmine flower.

DU9.claim: Madurai airport is about 12 km from the city.

evidence.quote: is located 12 kilometres from the city.

DU10.claim: Nearby are Tirupparankundram's rock-cut Murugan shrine, Azhagar Kovil at the foot of the Alagar Hills, and Koodal Azhagar in the city.

evidence.quote: Journey to Tirupparankundram, the auspicious abode of Lord Murugan, carved out of rock
a sacred abode dedicated to Lord Vishnu at the foothills of the majestic Alagar Hills.
Located in Madurai city, Koodal Azhagar temple is known for its brilliant architecture and design

DU11.claim: Karaikudi and Kanadukathan, in Chettinad, are nearby for mansions and food.

evidence.quote: Journey to Kaanadukathan and Karaikudi nearby to discover the enchanting heritage of the Chettinads

DU12.claim: Madurai has a hot tropical climate.

evidence.quote: Madurai has a hot tropical climate.

overview.text:
Madurai is called Thoonga Nagaram, 'the city that never sleeps', and it is one of the oldest cities in India, with references going back to the 3rd century BC. It was the seat of the Tamil Sangam, the assemblies of Tamil poets, and Incredible India calls it the Athens of the East.

The city grew around the Meenakshi Amman Temple, whose 14 towers of 45–50 m and thousand-pillared hall still dominate the old centre. Nearby are Thirumalai Nayak's palace of 1635, with 248 pillars and an evening light and sound show, the Gandhi Memorial Museum, and the Vandiyur Teppakulam, the state's largest temple tank. Festivals fill the calendar, from Pongal and Jallikattu in January to the Chithirai wedding festival in April–May. Come for the food too: jigarthanda, kari dosai and late-night kothu parotta. December to February is the most comfortable time.
